Supplement to “Multi-armed bandits with arriving arms: sequential screening and reliable set maintenance” October 15, 2026 Notation and scope The observation model has independent arm streams, each consisting of independent, identically distributed rewards in [0, 1], deterministic permanent arrivals A t , and one observation per physical time step. Let r ∗ (t) = max i∈A t r i , ∆ i (t) = r ∗ (t) − r i , and G t ε = {i : ∆ i (t) ≤ ε}. Reports are issued after the current observation and partition A t as (P t , N t , V t ). Write E lab = {∀t : P t ⊆ G t ε ⊆ A t \ N t }, U T (η) = X X 1{i ∈ V t , |∆ i (t) − ε| > η}, t≤T i∈A t and R T = t≤T ∆ I t (t). Reliability means P (E lab ) ≥ 1 − δ for every allowed environment. R Θ (a) minimizes worst-case ER T over full-model reliable policies with P θ (E lab , U T ≤ a) ≥ 1 − δ for all θ ∈ Θ. A bar denotes averaging under the independent uniform prior on all candidate signs. These priors are proof devices and impose no Bayesian requirement on the policy. All probability and sample-budget interfaces are proved below. Classical change of measure and multiple-recovery scales are credited to the existing literature (Kaufmann et al., 2016; Malloy and Nowak, 2014; Jamieson and Jain, 2018; Mason et al., 2020). P S1 A fixed-budget analysis of the screening-based UCB-AA proce- dure S1.1 Exact scope and executable conventions Fix a deterministic physical horizon T ≥ 1 and 0 < δ < 1. There are finitely many available arms by every finite time, at least one arm is available at time one, and arrivals are deterministic and permanent. The arm streams are independent, and each consists of iid [0, 1]-valued rewards with mean r i . The proof also applies conditionally on an independent exogenous arrival schedule. No gap-stability or cumulative-jump assumption is imposed. The learner observes the arrivals before selecting the arm at each physical time. Newly arriving arms are buffered until the next algorithmic round. All observations are retained, and an eliminated arm is not sampled again. (2) The calibration in (1) is a sufficient choice for this theorem; the smaller empirical calibration in the submitted version is not covered by this probability guarantee. Write s m for the physical starting time of algorithmic round m, with s 0 = 1. At s m admit every arm in the buffer, including arrivals at s m . The admitted batch is A m , its cumulative union is A(m), the incumbent survivors are C m−1 , and the initial active set is B m = C m−1 ∪ A m . Put C −1 = ∅. These are the round-based sets of the original UCB-AA procedure. Its notation K(m), when used, denotes a prescribed nondecreasing upper bound on |A(m)|; it is different from the actual physical-time count K t = |A t |. This proof does not require K(m) as an additional input because the calibration controls at most T observed streams. The following conventions make the original two-stage architecture precise. They are part of the analyzed procedure, not conclusions about unspecified implementations. 1. An elimination call at phase p first samples every arm in its candidate set S until its lifetime count reaches n p . An arm already at or above that target receives no additional sample. After the entire call’s sampling is complete, form LCB i (p) = r̂ i (n p ) − b p , UCB i (p) = r̂ i (n p ) + b p from the actual first n p observations of each reference arm. Remove simultaneously from S exactly those arms for which UCB i (p) < max LCB j (p). j∈R In particular, the inequality is strict. Prefix statistics for incumbents are retained; an unobserved prefix is never substituted into a comparison. 2. For m ≥ 2, run preliminary phases p = 0, . . . , m −2 on the surviving part of A m , with reference set equal to that part together with C m−1 . Only new arms are removed in these calls. Then run formal phases p = m − 1, m on the merged survivors. For m = 1, run only formal phases 0, 1; for m = 0, run formal phase 0. 3. If a new batch is empty, all its preliminary phases are no-ops: the set entering formal phase m − 1 is C m−1 . An empty surviving new batch is handled the same way. This specifies the missing intermediate set in the original pseudocode when preliminary screening is skipped. 4. Sampling orders and ties are fixed by observed history and independent policy randomization. Every physical pull counts toward T . Stop immediately after pull T , even in the middle of S-2 an arm’s target, an elimination call, or a round. No terminal round is appended to remove buffered arrivals from the regret ledger. Thus the alteration preserves buffering, screening against incumbent evidence, and formal elimination. It repairs the statistical bookkeeping and stopping convention; it does not replace UCB-AA by a reward-service mixture or by CP-UCB-AA. The original fixed-gap illustration can be expressed on the exogenous physical clock: release an optimal arm of mean 3/4 and an arm of mean 1/4 at time one, and at deterministic physical times τ i release arms of means r i = 1/2 − 2 −i−2 , i ≥ 1. The release times here are external physical times, not algorithmic round indices chosen after seeing the procedure’s random duration. S1.4 A physical-time doubling wrapper For completeness an unknown horizon can be handled by restarting at physical times 1, 2, 4, . . .. Epoch ℓ ≥ 0 has prescribed length h ℓ = 2 ℓ and local failure budget δ ℓ = δ/(2h 2 ℓ ). At its start, initialize UCB-AA with all currently available arms as its initial batch, empty local counts, and the calibration (1) for horizon h ℓ and failure budget δ ℓ . Previously eliminated arms re-enter. Use only new rewards for this epoch’s prefix statistics. Within the epoch, retain the two original stages and S-7 buffer new arrivals until the next local round. Stop the last epoch at the actual physical endpoint T . This is a standard physical-budget restart, distinct from completing geometrically many algorithmic rounds regardless of their random duration. Let D T dbl sum the arrival-delay terms of these epochs, with each epoch’s unfinished local round truncated at its epoch endpoint or at T . Put L T = 2 log(128T 4 /δ) + 1. The total exceptional-event contribution is at most X ℓ≥0 h ℓ δ ℓ = δ X −ℓ 2 = δ. 2 ℓ≥0 Add the nonnegative expected delay terms and use R T ≤ T . Audit and boundaries of the repair. The proof uses only bounded-stream concentration, strict interval comparisons, the roundwise survivor-count invariant, a finite sum, and Cauchy– Schwarz; each dependency is proved above. The competing route of terminal-gap compression is unnecessary and is not reinstated. Ties, empty new batches, the first two rounds, singleton active sets, deterministic rewards, arbitrary within-round benchmark jumps, and an unfinished first or last target are all covered. The historical-deficit term vanishes only on the common confidence event. The delay term is retained explicitly, including at the endpoint. The unknown-horizon wrapper restarts the original screening algorithm and does not claim history retention across epochs. Neither result establishes that the original smaller empirical calibration has the same error probability, that the withdrawn gap-dependent corollary is true, or that the old round-based online theorem has been repaired without changing its clock. S2 Proofs of the retained regret lower bounds These arguments use the original regret criterion R T (π; ν) = Tt=1 (r ∗ (t) − r I t ) at a deterministic physical horizon. Reward laws are stationary and independent across arms and draws. The policies are nonanticipating, may use independent randomization, and use the same action kernels in every environment being compared. Each comparison keeps the deterministic arrival schedule fixed. The schedules and reward laws may depend on T where this is explicitly stated. All logarithms are natural. S12 A horizon-truncated lower bound across compatible task win- dows Proposition S12.1 (Additive truncated area in one compatible experiment). Consider finitely many batches indexed by e. Batch e contains m e independent signs and has a deterministic validity window W e of length H e that begins at that batch’s arrival round. During that window each sign is its arm’s relative-goodness label and its boundary distance exceeds η. The signs across all batches are independent, other distributions do not encode them, and no information about batch e is available before its arrival. Samples remain interleaved and adaptive. Suppose every sign configuration has familywise reporting error at most 0 < δ ≤ 1/16. Let 0 < κ e < ∞ bound the two directional S-26 divergences in batch e, and define   h e = min H e , m e log(m e /δ) − 1 , 1024κ e   S = X m e h e . e When S > 0, one fixed full sign configuration satisfies P {U T (η) ≥ S/8} ≥ 1/7, provided every selected window lies before T and every candidate–time pair is counted only once. The windows may overlap when they concern distinct arms and their stated qualification structure is jointly realizable. Proof. At the rth round after batch e arrives, r ≤ h e , the entire experiment has supplied at most r samples of that batch. The contrapositive of the partial-recovery lemma shows that at least half the batch is determinate with probability less than 1/2. Its expected unresolved count is therefore at least m e /4. Let Y sum unresolved candidate–time pairs over the first h e rounds of all selected windows. All these pairs have boundary distance larger than η, so Y ≤ U T (η), while 0 ≤ Y ≤ S and EY ≥ S/4. If p = P (Y ≥ S/8), then S/4 ≤ S/8 + (7S/8)p, giving p ≥ 1/7. Select a fixed configuration from the common product prior. Compatibility of the windows is essential: this proof cannot sum bounds from mutually incompatible reference environments. S15 Additional computational details The main reporting-comparison table reports six methods; its cost-area figure includes all nine. These reporting experiments concern CP-UCB-AA and its comparators, not the repaired two-stage UCB-AA procedure. The allocation table below records every service variant. The full configuration lists each arm’s arrival time and mean, the shared potential reward construction, fixed policy parameters, and seeds. The actual final arm count and endpoint are used by the evaluator, not supplied to a policy. All methods receive the same observed-history information. The natural ALL-ε comparator is fully specified by the released code and is not claimed to reproduce FAREAST or (ST) 2 . The compiled CP reference was compared to its original public class for 20,000 successive steps, checking choices, service flags, counts and reports. The experiment records include per-run coverage and label errors, checkpoint completion, service regret, and the three-part regret identity. Their largest decomposition discrepancy was below 3.1 × 10 −12 . These checks validate the numerical implementation and accounting; they are not formal probability certificates or proofs of the analytical lower bounds.
